To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel non-parametric latent class mixture decomposition can be used to estimate the proportion of positives in a typical diagnostic assay where the proportion of positives is unknown, but where the probability of positivity is a monotonic function (usually linear) of the measurement of the activity.

a novel latent class model can provide a precise and unbiased estimate of the proportion of positive cells in an assay when the distribution of x values for positive cells is unknown, provided that the distribution of x has a moderate degree of separation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the estimation of the proportion of positive cases in an experimental assay, when the assay is known to have poor resolution, and the data consist of a sample of negative control cases and a sample of cases that are known to be positive.
the problem of estimating a proportion of positive objects in a population, based on the distribution of a continuous measure of biological activity (x) that has been measured for the population.

the problem of estimating a positivity from a continuous variable x that measures some form of biological or clinical activity, where the distribution of x among the positive objects is unknown but where the risk of positivity increases monotonically with x.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed non-parametric decomposition of the data is the best method for estimating the proportion of positives in a diagnostic assay with poor resolution.

the proposed non-parametric decomposition of a latent class model, using the method of maximum penalized likelihood estimation, provides an accurate and precise estimate of the proportion of positives, when the distribution of x is unknown, but where the risk of positivity increases as a monotonically increasing function of x.

the non-parametric mixture decomposition using a latent variable is a robust and powerful method for estimating the proportion of positives in a diagnostic test where the positive objects have a distribution of x that overlaps with the negative distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methods presented in this paper provide a useful framework for analysing data from a wide variety of diagnostic assays where the resolution of the assay is poor.

the latent class approach is the most robust estimator for a range of distributions of x, but that logistic regression provides a close approximation when the positive and negative distributions of x are well separated.

we have provided a new approach to the problem of estimating proportions of positive objects in diagnostic assays where:(i) x has been obtained from a set of negative controls, and (ii) x has been observed to be distributed with a moderate degree overlap between the negative and positive populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of a large amount of background noise, it is possible to estimate positivity with reasonable precision using a latent class mixture decomposition.
, when the proportion of positive samples is small, the use of a non-parametric latent class model is recommended for estimation of the proportion of positive observations.
when the proportion of positives is small and the distribution of x is poorly characterized, a nonparametric mixture decomposition can provide an unbiased estimator of the positivity.
